question: How do I create a FuzedFlow account?
answer_short: Create your company account from the FuzedFlow sign-up page using email and password or Google sign-in.
answer_long: New company accounts can be created with email/password or Google sign-in. New sign-ups start a 14-day free trial. If you were invited to an existing company, use the invitation flow instead of creating another company.

question: How long is the FuzedFlow free trial?
answer_short: New company accounts start with a 14-day free trial.
answer_long: New company accounts start with a 14-day free trial.

question: Can I sign in or sign up with Google?
answer_short: Yes. FuzedFlow supports Google authentication as well as email and password.
answer_long: Yes. FuzedFlow supports Google authentication as well as email and password.

question: Can the same email belong to more than one FuzedFlow company?
answer_short: No. The current account flow allows one FuzedFlow company per email address.
answer_long: If an invited email already belongs to another FuzedFlow company, FuzedFlow asks the administrator to invite a different email address.

question: Can I add a client message and terms to a change order?
answer_short: Yes. Change orders support client-facing messaging and terms.
answer_long: Yes. Change orders support client-facing messaging and terms.

question: Can I search change orders?
answer_short: Yes. Change orders can be searched by title, change-order number or client and filtered by status.
answer_long: Yes. Change orders can be searched by title, change-order number or client and filtered by status.

question: What statuses are available for change orders?
answer_short: The change-order list can filter Draft, Sent, Approved, Declined, and Invoiced records.
answer_long:
The **Change Orders** list offers status filters for **Draft**, **Sent**, **Approved**, **Declined**, and **Invoiced**, plus **All Statuses**.

Review status separately from financial totals and document delivery. The builder's **Mark as Sent** action changes the record's status without sending an email. Use the builder's send action when you need to contact the client.

Public client approval saves Approved status and the selected items/totals. It uses a different path from the builder's project synchronization action, so verify the project's budget and work records separately after a decision.

question: Can I see pending and approved change-order totals?
answer_short: Yes. The change-order area shows Pending Approval and Approved totals.
answer_long: Yes. The change-order area shows Pending Approval and Approved totals.

question: Can I send a change order to a client for approval?
answer_short: Open the saved change order builder and use Actions → Send via Email. The list-level Send to Client action is a coming-soon placeholder.
answer_long:
1. Open **Change Orders** and select the saved change order's number to open its builder.
2. Review the linked project, client, scope, line items, and totals, then save.
3. Use **Actions → Client Preview** to check the client document.
4. Choose **Actions → Send via Email**, review the client address, subject, message, signature, and optional PDF attachment, then select **Send Email**.
5. Wait for the send result before assuming the message was dispatched.

The builder also has **Send via Text Message** and a client review link. The list-level **Send to Client** action currently displays a coming-soon notice. **Mark as Sent** changes status without sending a message; Sent alone does not prove delivery to the recipient's inbox.

Approval and request changes are separate client actions. After approval, check project-budget synchronization separately.

question: What can a client access through the Client Portal?
answer_short: The Client Portal provides access to client-facing documents such as quotes, change orders and invoices when the portal is enabled.
answer_long:
Clients can use their shared portal link to access client-facing documents such as quotes, change orders, and invoices when the portal is enabled.

Company staff control which project phases, updates, and files are client-visible. Review client-visible information before sharing access; internal records are managed separately.

question: Can I disable the Client Portal?
answer_short: Yes. Company settings include a control for enabling or disabling the Client Portal.
answer_long: Yes. Company settings include a control for enabling or disabling the Client Portal.

question: Can I customize the Client Portal welcome message?
answer_short: Yes. The Client Portal settings include a custom welcome message.
answer_long: Yes. The Client Portal settings include a custom welcome message.

question: What appears in the Client Timeline Feed?
answer_short: The Client Timeline combines client-visible manual updates, milestones, project phases and client-visible issues into one chronological feed.
answer_long: The Client Timeline combines client-visible manual updates, milestones, project phases and client-visible issues into one chronological feed.

question: Can clients see internal notes or micro-costs in the Client Timeline?
answer_short: No. The Client Timeline is designed to show client-visible project information while keeping internal notes and micro-costs hidden.
answer_long: No. The Client Timeline is designed to show client-visible project information while keeping internal notes and micro-costs hidden.

question: Can I post a manual project update for the client?
answer_short: Yes. Use Post Update in the project Client View to save a dated title, details, and client-visibility choice.
answer_long:
1. Open **PM Projects**, select **Open** on the project, and choose **Client View**.
2. Select **Post Update**, or **Post First Update** when the feed is empty.
3. Enter **Event Title / Summary**, **Event Date**, and **Details & Notes**.
4. Review **Visible to Client** and select **Post Update** to save.

The dialog does not include a category selector; manual posts use the Update category. Updates with client visibility switched off are not shown in the client-visible feed. Saving an update does not itself confirm delivery of an email or text.

question: Can I upload files to a client record?
answer_short: Yes. FuzedFlow supports client attachments including site photos/information and subcontractor quotes.
answer_long: Yes. FuzedFlow supports client attachments including site photos/information and subcontractor quotes.

question: Where can I keep site photos before a project starts?
answer_short: Site photos and project information can be uploaded to the client's record and stored as client attachments.
answer_long: Site photos and project information can be uploaded to the client's record and stored as client attachments.

question: Can I create tasks for a client?
answer_short: Yes. Client records can include tasks with status, priority, due date, estimated hours, project link and assignee.
answer_long: Yes. Client records can include tasks with status, priority, due date, estimated hours, project link and assignee.

question: Do subcontractors need a FuzedFlow account to view the Contractor Portal?
answer_short: No. The project has a public Contractor Portal link that can be shared with bidding subcontractors or temporary workers without requiring an account.
answer_long: No. The project has a public Contractor Portal link that can be shared with bidding subcontractors or temporary workers without requiring an account.

question: Can I remove a file from the Contractor Portal?
answer_short: Yes. Files can be removed from the portal's visible file list.
answer_long: Yes. Files can be removed from the portal's visible file list.

question: Can I control the scope of work shown to contractors?
answer_short: Yes. The Contractor Portal tab includes a Scope of Work editor for project instructions and expectations.
answer_long: Yes. The Contractor Portal tab includes a Scope of Work editor for project instructions and expectations.

question: Can I share an existing project document with subcontractors?
answer_short: Yes. You can select existing project documents or plans and add them to the Contractor Portal without uploading the file again.
answer_long:
1. Open the project’s **Contractor Portal** tab.
2. Choose the existing project documents or plans that contractors should see.
3. Review the visible file list and scope before sharing the portal link.

The public portal does not require a FuzedFlow account. Share only documents intended for the contractors receiving the link.

question: Can I upload files directly to the Contractor Portal?
answer_short: Yes. You can upload new files directly to the portal and optionally add a description.
answer_long: Yes. You can upload new files directly to the portal and optionally add a description.

question: Can project Daily Logs be edited or deleted?
answer_short: Authorized office/project staff can edit or delete daily logs. The Employee Portal personal log list offers Details and Delete, but no full edit form.
answer_long:
Authorized office/project staff can edit and delete entries in **PM Projects → your project → Project Notes**, or the office **Daily Logs** page. Review the log’s date, author, and linked work before changing it.

In **Employee Portal → Project Notes**, your personal log history provides **Details** and a delete action with confirmation. It does not provide the office’s full Edit Log form. Ask the manager how to correct an important submitted report instead of assuming you can edit it directly or deleting it prematurely.

Deleting a log removes the record; it does not reverse inventory usage mentioned in its Materials Used text. Inventory transactions are managed separately.

question: What information belongs in a Daily Log?
answer_short: Daily Logs are designed to capture the date, weather, crew on site, work summary, blockers, safety concerns, materials used and photos.
answer_long:
Use a daily log to record the date, weather, crew, work completed, blockers, safety concerns, materials, and photos.

For a project, open **PM Projects → your project → Project Notes**. Field users can use **Employee Portal → Project Notes** when enabled.

Write clear factual updates and check the linked project before saving. The main **Daily Logs** page also has **Submit New Log** for creating a field log.

question: What weather options are available in a Daily Log?
answer_short: The PM Daily Log component includes Sunny, Cloudy, Rainy, Snowy, Windy, Hot and Cold.
answer_long: The PM Daily Log component includes Sunny, Cloudy, Rainy, Snowy, Windy, Hot and Cold.

question: What can employees access in the Employee Portal?
answer_short: The Employee Portal provides attendance, expenses, assigned projects, schedule, tasks, project notes, and inventory where the plan and company modules allow. Self-service Profile setup is incomplete.
answer_long:
Open **Employee Portal** for your personal field tools. Available sections depend on the company’s plan and enabled features.

- **Clock In**, **My Time Sheets**, **My Pay**, **My Time Off**, and **My Expenses**.
- **My Projects**, **My Schedule**, **Project Notes**, **My Tasks**, and **Inventory**.

On mobile, select **More** to find the full menu. If a section is missing, ask an owner or administrator to check **Settings → Employee Portal** and the company’s HR plan access.

The **Profile → Set Up Profile** self-service save is currently incomplete. Ask an owner or administrator to correct your name, role, hourly rate, or account activity through **Settings → Team Management**; use the employer’s HR process for other employee information. Do not rely on the incomplete form as the sole record for emergency contact details.

question: What can administrators approve in the HR area?
answer_short: Owners, administrators, and office staff with HR plan access can review time entries, time-off requests, and expenses. Use All Statuses to find Submitted expenses.
answer_long:
Open **Human Resources** as an Owner, Admin, or Office user on a plan with HR access. Choose **Timesheets**, **Time Off**, or **Expenses**; on mobile use the view dropdown.

1. Check the employee, status, and date filters.
2. Review the hours or amount and supporting details.
3. Select the intended records and choose **Approve** or **Reject**.
4. Use **Adjust** on an existing timesheet to correct its date, hours, timestamps, type, status, and notes.

Employee expense claims begin as **Submitted**. HR’s default **Pending Only** filter matches Pending or blank status, so it can hide Submitted claims. Select **All Statuses** and an appropriate date range to find them.

Approving a record changes its status; it does not pay wages or issue an expense reimbursement. My Pay shows estimates, and final processing follows the employer’s payroll process.

question: Does Inventory support CSV functionality?
answer_short: Yes. The Inventory page includes CSV-related functionality.
answer_long: Yes. The Inventory page includes CSV-related functionality.

question: What can FuzedFlow track in Inventory?
answer_short: Warehouse Inventory tracks physical items, quantity, unit, cost, location, reorder threshold, and supplier details; Usage Report shows saved movements.
answer_long:
**Inventory → Warehouse Inventory** tracks physical stock records including item name, SKU, category, unit, unit cost, current quantity, physical location, reorder threshold, supplier, description, and image.

The **Low Stock Alerts** filter is calculated from quantity at or below the reorder threshold. It is not a separate editable purchasing-status field.

Use **Usage Report** to inspect saved **Consume** and **Receive** transactions and filter by project, employee, or type. A direct Current Qty edit is different from recording a project-specific usage transaction.

Project **Materials** has separate purchasing states such as To Order, Ordered, and Received. Saving project materials or a purchase order does not automatically change warehouse stock.

question: Can I delete a payment milestone after it has been paid?
answer_short: The current invoice builder does not protect paid milestones from removal. Do not remove paid milestones without reviewing the payment ledger and allocation.
answer_long:
The current **Invoice Builder → Payment Schedule** shows a remove action for milestones, including paid ones. Do not rely on a paid milestone being protected from deletion.

Before changing the schedule, review **Payments History** and which payments are allocated to each milestone. Removing a milestone is not a refund and can make the schedule inconsistent with its payment history. Ask the authorized billing user or support to review the invoice if a paid milestone needs correction.

question: Can I customize the invoice email?
answer_short: Yes. The invoice email can use company templates and supports variables such as client name, invoice number and invoice title.
answer_long: Yes. The invoice email can use company templates and supports variables such as client name, invoice number and invoice title.

question: Can I accidentally delete the payment link while editing the invoice text message?
answer_short: The secure invoice link is displayed separately from the editable message and is appended to the outgoing SMS.
answer_long: The secure invoice link is displayed separately from the editable message and is appended to the outgoing SMS.

question: What invoice statuses does FuzedFlow use?
answer_short: Invoice workflows use Draft, Sent, Partial, Paid and Overdue statuses.
answer_long: Invoice workflows use Draft, Sent, Partial, Paid and Overdue statuses.

question: Can a payment milestone include a trigger or requirement?
answer_short: Yes. Each milestone can include a requirement such as 'Upon contract signing', 'After drywall inspection' or another custom trigger.
answer_long: Yes. Each milestone can include a requirement such as 'Upon contract signing', 'After drywall inspection' or another custom trigger.

question: Can I create a payment schedule for an invoice?
answer_short: Yes. Invoice payment schedules are built from named payment milestones with dollar amounts and trigger/requirement descriptions.
answer_long: Yes. Invoice payment schedules are built from named payment milestones with dollar amounts and trigger/requirement descriptions.

question: Why can't I confirm an invoice payment schedule?
answer_short: In the current invoice builder, add or edit milestones with Save Item and then save the invoice; there is no separate Confirm Schedule action in that screen.
answer_long:
In the current **Invoice Builder**, use **Payment Schedule → Add Milestone**, enter the name, event and amount, and select **Save Item**. Then save the invoice and verify the stored schedule.

Review the sum of the milestone amounts against the invoice contract total. The builder rejects a new or edited milestone that would exceed the available total and can adjust an unpaid milestone after the contract total changes. Recheck every amount after scope or price edits.

Do not assume paid milestones are protected from removal in the current builder. Preserve their allocation and ledger history. If invoice saving fails, keep your entered details and inspect the invoice list before retrying; contact support if it remains unresolved.

question: How do I send an invoice by email?
answer_short: Use Send Invoice via Email. The message includes a secure View & Pay Invoice link and an Access Client Portal link, then marks the invoice Sent after a successful send.
answer_long:
Open the invoice, choose its email sending action, and review the client’s address, subject, message, and secure **View & Pay Invoice** link. Send after confirming the invoice details.

A successful send updates the invoice to **Sent**. The client portal link is included where supported. Do not treat opening the send dialog as confirmation of delivery.

question: Can I send an invoice by text message?
answer_short: Yes. FuzedFlow can send the client an SMS with the invoice number, balance due and a secure Public Invoice link.
answer_long: Yes. FuzedFlow can send the client an SMS with the invoice number, balance due and a secure Public Invoice link.

question: Can I assign a lead to a team member?
answer_short: Yes. Leads can be assigned to a team member for follow-up and sales ownership.
answer_long:
1. Open the lead in **Lead Tracker**.
2. Open the lead’s editing form.
3. Choose the person under **Assign Team Member**.
4. Save the change.

An assigned sales owner helps your team track follow-up responsibility; it does not automatically create a separate task.

question: What happens when I convert a lead to a client?
answer_short: Conversion creates a client and marks the lead Won. Lead Detail and the tracker’s Won confirmation transfer different information, so review the resulting client.
answer_long:
From **Lead Detail**, choose **Convert to Client** when the prospect should become a client. That workflow creates a client, marks the lead **Won**, copies lead notes and files, and attempts to link the lead’s quotes to the new client. Review the resulting client’s contact details, addresses, attachments and quotes.

The **Lead Tracker → Won** confirmation also creates a client, but its transfer is more limited: it copies contact/address information and a description-or-notes field rather than the full detail history. Do not assume the two routes transfer identical data.

Conversion does not merge into an existing client. Search Clients first, and inspect the result before repeating a failed conversion so you do not create duplicates.

question: Can I import or export leads?
answer_short: Yes. The leads area includes import and export functionality.
answer_long: Yes. The leads area includes import and export functionality.

question: What information can I store on a lead?
answer_short: Lead records can include contact details, address, description, internal notes, priority, estimated value, next follow-up date, assigned team member and files.
answer_long:
Open **Lead Tracker** and select **New Lead**. Enter the required first name and surname, then add email, phone, source, priority, pipeline stage, estimated value, next follow-up date, and **Assign Team Member** as needed.

Add the site address, description, photos, and internal notes before selecting **Create Lead**. Review the lead after saving to confirm the details.

question: Can I set a follow-up date on a lead?
answer_short: Yes. A lead can have a next follow-up date so the sales team can track when to contact the prospect again.
answer_long:
Open the lead’s editing form, enter **Next Follow Up Date**, and save. Use the lead details and filters to review when the prospect should be contacted again.

A saved follow-up date is a planning field; it does not by itself send a message to the prospect.

question: Can I view leads as a list instead of a Kanban board?
answer_short: Yes. FuzedFlow supports both Kanban and list views for lead tracking.
answer_long:
In **Lead Tracker**, use the view controls to switch between **Kanban** and **List**. Kanban groups leads by stage; List makes it easier to compare lead details.

Use search and the available filters to narrow the records shown. Switching views does not change a lead’s pipeline stage.

question: Do lead notes transfer when I convert a lead to a client?
answer_short: Lead Detail conversion copies dedicated lead-note records. The tracker’s Won confirmation transfers only limited description/notes information.
answer_long:
It depends on the conversion route.

- **Lead Detail → Convert to Client** copies the lead’s dedicated note records to the new client, along with its description/internal notes and other transferred information.
- The **Lead Tracker → Won** confirmation copies a description-or-notes value into the new client; it does not perform the same dedicated-note history transfer.

After conversion, open **Client Detail** and verify the notes and attachments you need. Keep the original lead while resolving an incomplete transfer, and do not repeat conversion solely to recover a missing note because it can create another client.

question: What stages are available in the FuzedFlow lead pipeline?
answer_short: The lead pipeline includes New, Contacted, Booked Visit, Quoted, Negotiation, Won and Lost.
answer_long:
The pipeline stages are **New, Contacted, Booked Visit, Quoted, Negotiation, Won, and Lost**.

Move the lead as the sales conversation progresses. **Won** and **Lost** are closing outcomes. Updating a stage does not send a quote or invoice to the client.

question: How do I move a lead to another pipeline stage?
answer_short: Use the lead pipeline to update the lead's stage. In Kanban view, leads can be moved through the sales stages.
answer_long: Use the lead pipeline to update the lead's stage. In Kanban view, leads can be moved through the sales stages.

question: Can I apply a payment to a specific scheduled milestone?
answer_short: Yes. Select the scheduled payment and FuzedFlow automatically fills the amount still due on that milestone.
answer_long: Yes. Select the scheduled payment and FuzedFlow automatically fills the amount still due on that milestone.

question: When does an invoice become Paid?

answer_long: After payment records are recalculated, the invoice becomes Paid when its remaining balance reaches zero.

question: How are payment milestone statuses calculated?
answer_short: Each milestone becomes Pending, Partial or Paid based on the total payments linked to that milestone.
answer_long: Each milestone becomes Pending, Partial or Paid based on the total payments linked to that milestone.

question: Can FuzedFlow track partial payments?
answer_short: Yes. If some money has been received but a balance remains, the invoice status becomes Partial.
answer_long: Yes. If some money has been received but a balance remains, the invoice status becomes Partial.

question: What manual payment methods can I record?
answer_short: The payment recorder includes Bank Transfer, Credit Card, Check, Cash and Other.
answer_long: The payment recorder includes Bank Transfer, Credit Card, Check, Cash and Other.

question: Can I store a cheque number or payment reference?
answer_short: Yes. Record Payment includes a Reference Notes field for items such as cheque/check numbers or Stripe references.
answer_long: Yes. Record Payment includes a Reference Notes field for items such as cheque/check numbers or Stripe references.

question: What information appears on the payment receipt?
answer_short: The receipt includes payment dates, invoice numbers, payment methods, payment amounts and the total amount received.
answer_long: The receipt includes payment dates, invoice numbers, payment methods, payment amounts and the total amount received.

question: Can a receipt include payments from more than one invoice?
answer_short: Yes. The receipt can include selected payments from different invoices belonging to the same client.
answer_long: Yes. The receipt can include selected payments from different invoices belonging to the same client.

question: Can one receipt include multiple payments?
answer_short: Yes. You can select multiple recorded payments for the same client and send them together on one receipt.
answer_long: Yes. You can select multiple recorded payments for the same client and send them together on one receipt.

question: How do I record a client payment?
answer_short: Open Record Payment, choose the payment date, amount and payment method, optionally link it to a scheduled milestone, then save the payment.
answer_long:
1. Open **Record Payment** for the invoice.
2. Enter the payment date, amount received, and payment method.
3. Add a reference such as a cheque number if useful.
4. Choose a scheduled milestone or apply the payment to the overall balance.
5. Save and review the updated invoice balance.

Record only payments you have actually received; the form records a payment rather than charging a card.

question: Can I email a payment receipt to a client?
answer_short: Yes. FuzedFlow can generate and email a PDF payment receipt.
answer_long:
Select the client and the recorded payments to include in the receipt. You can combine multiple payments from that client’s invoices.

Review the recipient and selected transactions before sending the generated PDF receipt. Sending a receipt does not record a new payment.

question: What drawing categories are available?
answer_short: Plans & Elevations supports Floor Plan, Elevation, Site Plan, Electrical, Plumbing, Mechanical, Structural, Detail Drawing, As-Built and Other.
answer_long: Plans & Elevations supports Floor Plan, Elevation, Site Plan, Electrical, Plumbing, Mechanical, Structural, Detail Drawing, As-Built and Other.

answer_long: Yes. Plans & Elevations includes a download action for the stored file.

question: Can I preview uploaded plans?
answer_short: Image-based plan files can be previewed in a large lightbox. Other files can be opened in a new browser tab.
answer_long:
Open **PM Projects → your project → Plans & Elevations**, then choose the drawing. Image files open in a larger preview. Other file types can open in a new browser tab.

Use the download action to save a copy. Check the revision/version before sharing drawings with a trade.

question: Can I record a revision or version on a plan?
answer_short: Yes. Each plan/elevation record can include a Revision / Version value and content notes.
answer_long: Yes. Each plan/elevation record can include a Revision / Version value and content notes.

question: Can Pricebook items have categories and subcategories?
answer_short: Yes. Pricebook items support main category, subcategory and a third category level.
answer_long: Yes. Pricebook items support main category, subcategory and a third category level.

question: What information can I store in a Pricebook item?
answer_short: Pricebook items can include name, categories, unit, material cost, labour cost, total cost, margin, client price, description, SKU, supplier, supplier URL, tax status and an image.
answer_long: Pricebook items can include name, categories, unit, material cost, labour cost, total cost, margin, client price, description, SKU, supplier, supplier URL, tax status and an image.

question: Can I add a Pricebook item directly to a quote phase?

answer_long: Yes. Quote phases include a Pricebook selector for adding saved products to the phase.

question: Can I save a quote line item to the Pricebook?
answer_short: Yes. A line item can be saved as a new Pricebook item directly from the quote builder.
answer_long: Yes. A line item can be saved as a new Pricebook item directly from the quote builder.

question: How do I import materials from a quote into a project?
answer_short: Use Import Quote in Project Materials. FuzedFlow finds the attached quote and imports quote line items that are flagged Track Material.
answer_long:
1. Open the project from **PM Projects**.
2. Choose **Materials**.
3. Select **Import Quote**.
4. Review the imported names, quantities, unit costs, suppliers, and phase assignments.

Only line items with **Track Material** enabled on the attached quote are imported. Matching material names are skipped to reduce duplicates.

question: How does FuzedFlow calculate a material's total estimated cost?
answer_short: Project Materials calculates total estimated cost as Quantity × Estimated Unit Cost.
answer_long: Project Materials calculates total estimated cost as Quantity × Estimated Unit Cost.

question: Does importing materials create duplicates?
answer_short: FuzedFlow checks existing project-material names and skips matching names during the quote import.
answer_long: FuzedFlow checks existing project-material names and skips matching names during the quote import.

question: What information comes across when I import a material from a quote?
answer_short: The import brings across the item name, description, quantity, unit, estimated unit cost and supplier.
answer_long: The import brings across the item name, description, quantity, unit, estimated unit cost and supplier.

question: Can I assign a material to a project phase?
answer_short: Yes. Materials can be linked to a project phase or left under General / Unassigned Materials.
answer_long: Yes. Materials can be linked to a project phase or left under General / Unassigned Materials.

question: What statuses are available for project materials?

answer_long: Project Materials uses To Order, Ordered and Received.

question: What can I track on a project material?
answer_short: Project materials can include material name, notes, phase, quantity, unit, estimated cost, supplier and order status.
answer_long: Project materials can include material name, notes, phase, quantity, unit, estimated cost, supplier and order status.

question: Why didn't a quote item import into Project Materials?
answer_short: Only quote line items flagged as materials are imported. Make sure Track Material is enabled on the quote item and that the project has an attached quote.
answer_long:
Check these items:

- The project is linked to the correct quote.
- **Track Material** is enabled on the quote line item.
- The quote changes were saved before importing.
- A project material with the same name has not already been imported.

Then return to the project’s **Materials** tab and use **Import Quote** again.

question: Can I assign a lead or foreman to a project phase?
answer_short: Yes. A project phase can be assigned to an internal team member as its Lead/Foreman.
answer_long: Yes. A project phase can be assigned to an internal team member as its Lead/Foreman.

question: Can I assign a subcontractor to a project phase?

question: Can I set a budget for a project phase?
answer_short: Yes. Project phases include a Phase Budget field and a Micro-Costing area for comparing tracked material costs against that budget.
answer_long: Yes. Project phases include a Phase Budget field and a Micro-Costing area for comparing tracked material costs against that budget.

question: Can I hide a project phase from the client?
answer_short: Yes. Expand the phase and switch Visible in Client Portal off; the visibility change saves directly.
answer_long:
1. Open **PM Projects**, select **Open** on the project, and choose **Phases**.
2. Expand the required phase with its chevron.
3. Change **Visible in Client Portal**. The switch saves the visibility change directly; there is no separate Save Phase button for this update.
4. Check **Client View** to review the visible phase feed.

Only make phases visible when their information is appropriate for the client. The feed displays phase name, progress, and status; Internal Phase Notes and Micro-Costing are separate operational sections.

question: Can I keep internal notes on a project phase?
answer_short: Yes. Project phases include internal notes for private instructions and reminders.
answer_long: Yes. Project phases include internal notes for private instructions and reminders.

question: How does FuzedFlow show an overdue project phase?
answer_short: If the target end date has passed and the phase is not Completed, FuzedFlow displays how many days overdue the phase is.
answer_long: If the target end date has passed and the phase is not Completed, FuzedFlow displays how many days overdue the phase is.

question: Can I track planned and actual dates for a project phase?
answer_short: Yes. Each phase can store Target Start, Target End, Actual Start and Actual End dates.
answer_long: Yes. Each phase can store Target Start, Target End, Actual Start and Actual End dates.

question: How is project-phase task progress calculated?
answer_short: The phase screen calculates progress from the number of linked tasks with Done status compared with the total linked tasks.
answer_long: The phase screen calculates progress from the number of linked tasks with Done status compared with the total linked tasks.

question: What statuses can a project phase have?
answer_short: Project phases support Not Started, In Progress, Blocked and Completed.
answer_long: Project phases support Not Started, In Progress, Blocked and Completed.

question: Can I create a subcontractor while editing a phase?
answer_short: Yes. The phase screen includes Quick Add for creating a new subcontractor and immediately assigning it to the phase.
answer_long: Yes. The phase screen includes Quick Add for creating a new subcontractor and immediately assigning it to the phase.

question: Can I create a project from a quote?
answer_short: FuzedFlow's project workflow can connect a project to a client and quote and can import quote phases and materials into the project workflow.
answer_long: FuzedFlow's project workflow can connect a project to a client and quote and can import quote phases and materials into the project workflow.

question: What can I manage inside a FuzedFlow project?
answer_short: Project workspaces include areas for overview, phases, client view/timeline, subcontractors, materials, staff and tasks, client notes, permits, quotes/documents, plans/elevations, contractor portal and project notes/daily logs.
answer_long:
Open **PM Projects**, select your project, and use the section selector to navigate.

The workspace includes **Overview, Phases, Client View, Phase Timeline, Subcontractors, Materials, Staff & Tasks, Client Notes, Permits, Quotes & Docs, Plans & Elevations, Contractor Portal, and Project Notes**.

On mobile, use the section selector near the project header. Choose **Staff & Tasks** to assign work or filter tasks by assignee.

question: Can I create a new vendor while making a purchase order?
answer_short: Yes. The purchase-order workflow supports creating a vendor during the PO process.
answer_long: Yes. The purchase-order workflow supports creating a vendor during the PO process.

question: What information can I include on a purchase order?
answer_short: Purchase orders can include vendor, project, order date, expected delivery date, shipping address, notes, terms and individual line items.
answer_long: Purchase orders can include vendor, project, order date, expected delivery date, shipping address, notes, terms and individual line items.

question: Can I generate a PDF purchase order?
answer_short: Yes. Purchase-order details include PDF generation.
answer_long: Yes. Purchase-order details include PDF generation.

answer_long: Yes. FuzedFlow includes a public vendor-facing purchase-order view.

question: How do I know if a client changed an optional item?
answer_short: FuzedFlow marks an optional phase or line item as CLIENT MODIFIED when the client's choice differs from the contractor's default selection.
answer_long: FuzedFlow marks an optional phase or line item as CLIENT MODIFIED when the client's choice differs from the contractor's default selection.

question: Can the client choose optional quote items before approving?
answer_short: Yes. Clients can change optional phase and line-item selections before the quote is approved.
answer_long: Their selections change the active subtotal, taxable amount, taxes and final quote total. Once the quote is Approved, those selections are locked.

question: What happens to the client price when I change a line item's cost?
answer_short: FuzedFlow recalculates the client price while maintaining the item's current margin when possible.
answer_long: If an existing valid cost/price margin is available, that margin is preserved. Otherwise FuzedFlow uses the company default margin.

question: What is the default margin on a new item?
answer_short: FuzedFlow uses the company's configured default margin. If no value is configured, the quote components fall back to 20%.
answer_long: FuzedFlow uses the company's configured default margin. If no value is configured, the quote components fall back to 20%.

question: Can I duplicate a quote line item?
answer_short: Yes. Individual line items can be duplicated.
answer_long: Yes. Individual line items can be duplicated.

question: Can I duplicate a quote phase?
answer_short: Yes. Duplicating a phase copies the phase and its line items.
answer_long: Yes. Duplicating a phase copies the phase and its line items.

question: Can I duplicate an existing quote for another client?
answer_short: Yes. Choose a client and duplicate the quote. FuzedFlow creates a new Draft and copies the quote phases, line items and pricing while clearing client-specific approval/view/signature data.
answer_long:
Use the quote’s duplication action and choose the client for the new estimate. FuzedFlow creates a **Draft** and copies phases, line items, and pricing.

Client-specific approval, viewing, and selection information is cleared. Review the new client, address, quantities, prices, and terms before sending the duplicate.

question: Does FuzedFlow calculate margin or markup?
answer_short: FuzedFlow's quote pricing uses gross margin, not markup.
answer_long:
FuzedFlow uses **gross margin**, not markup.

**Selling price = Cost ÷ (1 − Margin)**

For example, a $100 cost at a 20% margin gives a $125 selling price. A 20% markup would give $120, so the two methods produce different prices.

Changing the client price recalculates the margin. Review the resulting price and profit before saving.

question: Can I move a line item from one quote phase to another?
answer_short: Yes. Use the move action on the line item to select another phase.
answer_long: Yes. Use the move action on the line item to select another phase.

question: Can I make a quote line item optional?
answer_short: Yes. Mark the line item Optional. You can also choose whether it is Pre-select by default for the client.
answer_long: Yes. Mark the line item Optional. You can also choose whether it is Pre-select by default for the client.

question: Can I make an entire quote phase optional?
answer_short: Yes. A complete phase can be marked Optional and can also be pre-selected for the client.
answer_long: Yes. A complete phase can be marked Optional and can also be pre-selected for the client.

question: What happens if I manually change the client price?
answer_short: FuzedFlow recalculates the margin from the new selling price and the current unit cost.
answer_long: FuzedFlow recalculates the margin from the new selling price and the current unit cost.

question: Can I customize the quote email message?
answer_short: Yes. Quote email content and the company email signature can use templates from company settings.
answer_long: The quote email template supports variables such as client name, quote number and quote title.

question: Can I see a history of automatic quote follow-ups?
answer_short: The current Quote Builder does not display a per-quote automatic follow-up history or delivery-status panel.
answer_long:
The current **Quote Builder** does not show an automatic follow-up history panel with reminder number, recipient, subject, or delivery status.

Company reminder settings can be reviewed in **Admin Settings → Automations**, but a configured schedule or a quote’s **Sent** status is not proof that a specific reminder was delivered. Quote view tracking is a separate feature and should not be treated as reminder-delivery history.

If you need to confirm whether a reminder went out, ask the administrator or support to check the scheduled reminder process and email delivery using the quote number and approximate time. Do not repeatedly send a manual reminder before checking whether the customer already received one.

question: Can I customize the automatic quote follow-up email?
answer_short: The current quote reminder process does not provide a subscriber-editable per-quote follow-up subject or body template.
answer_long:
The current **Quote Builder** does not include a follow-up email-template editor. **Admin Settings → Automations** configures company reminder timing, while the implemented quote-reminder process uses its own reminder subject and message.

For a manually sent quote email, use **Actions → Send via Email** and edit its subject, message and signature before sending. That manual message editor is separate from automatic follow-ups. Ask support about a required reminder customization rather than assuming the ordinary quote email template changes the automated reminder.

question: Can FuzedFlow automatically follow up on sent quotes?
answer_short: Quote reminders are configured for the company under Admin Settings → Automations, not by a per-quote reminder control in the current builder.
answer_long:
Company quote-reminder settings are under **Admin Settings → Automations → Quote Follow-ups**. An authorized user can enable the company setting, review **First Check-in** and **Final Push**, and select **Save Automations**.

The implemented reminder process considers **Sent** or **Viewed** quotes linked to a client with an email address. Its timing uses the quote’s creation date, not the date you most recently sent it. Approved or Declined quotes are outside those reminder statuses.

The current Quote Builder does not offer per-quote reminder intervals, maximum-reminder settings, or a follow-up enable switch. Sending also depends on the deployed scheduled process and email setup; saving company settings alone is not proof that a reminder was delivered. Ask the administrator or support to verify reminder operation if needed.

question: Can I add notes to a quote that the client cannot see?
answer_short: Use quote-level or phase-level internal notes for saved private reminders, and verify them after saving. Do not rely on line-item notes persisting.
answer_long:
Use the quote’s **Internal Notes** or the phase’s private notes field under **Settings** for saved team reminders. These fields are separate from the client-facing scope and message. Save and reopen the quote to confirm the notes you need are retained.

The line-item editor also displays an internal-notes field, but the current quote-save workflow does not retain that field with the saved line item. Copy important line-item reminders into the quote or phase internal notes before saving. Do not put private information in the item description, which is shown to the client.

question: Can I add a photo to a quote line item?
answer_short: Yes. Individual quote line items can include an image.
answer_long: Yes. Individual quote line items can include an image.

question: What information can I enter on a quote line item?
answer_short: A quote line item can include quantity, unit, material cost, labour cost, total unit cost, client price, margin, tax status, supplier, material tracking, description, internal notes and a photo.
answer_long: A quote line item can include quantity, unit, material cost, labour cost, total unit cost, client price, margin, tax status, supplier, material tracking, description, internal notes and a photo.

question: What does 'Quote is Currently Locked' mean?
answer_short: Coordinate quote editing with your team; automatic editing locks are not active in the current Quote Builder.
answer_long: Do not rely on automatic editing protection in the current Quote Builder. Coordinate with your team so only one person edits a quote at a time, and save before handing it over.

question: Can I add photos to a quote phase?
answer_short: Yes. A quote phase can contain multiple inspiration or reference photos.
answer_long: Yes. A quote phase can contain multiple inspiration or reference photos.

question: Can I show a scope of work for each quote phase?
answer_short: Yes. Each phase has a client-facing Scope of Work field and a setting that controls whether the scope is shown on the quote.
answer_long: Yes. Each phase has a client-facing Scope of Work field and a setting that controls whether the scope is shown on the quote.

question: Can I see the estimated profit on a quote line item?
answer_short: Yes. The line-item editor displays estimated profit based on quantity, unit price and unit cost.
answer_long: Yes. The line-item editor displays estimated profit based on quantity, unit price and unit cost.

question: How do I send a quote by email?
answer_short: Use Send Quote via Email. FuzedFlow builds a branded email with the client's secure public quote link and marks the quote Sent after a successful send.
answer_long:
1. Open the quote in **Quote Builder**.
2. Review the client, scope, pricing, and terms; save your changes.
3. Open **Actions → Send via Email**.
4. Check the recipient, subject, message, and secure quote link.
5. Send the email.

The quote is marked **Sent** after a successful email send. Previewing a quote is not the same as sending it.

question: Can I send a quote by text message?
answer_short: Yes. FuzedFlow can send the quote by SMS with the secure Public Quote link appended to the message.
answer_long:
1. Open and save the quote.
2. Choose **Actions → Send via Text Message**.
3. Review the client’s phone number and message.
4. Send the text.

The secure public quote link is appended to the outgoing message. SMS availability depends on the company’s messaging setup.

question: Can I customize the quote text-message template?
answer_short: Yes. FuzedFlow can use the company's quote SMS template and replaces quote/client variables before sending.
answer_long: Yes. FuzedFlow can use the company's quote SMS template and replaces quote/client variables before sending.

question: Can I record the supplier for a quote item?
answer_short: Yes. When Track Material is enabled, the quote line item can store the supplier name.
answer_long: Yes. When Track Material is enabled, the quote line item can store the supplier name.

question: What units can I use on a quote line item?
answer_short: The quote builder includes units such as ea, ft, sqft, hr, lft, m, sqm, bag, box and roll.
answer_long: The quote builder includes units such as ea, ft, sqft, hr, lft, m, sqm, bag, box and roll.

question: Can I see whether a quote has been viewed?
answer_short: FuzedFlow records quote-view events and distinguishes internal views from client views.
answer_long: FuzedFlow records quote-view events and distinguishes internal views from client views.

question: Can I reorder line items inside a quote phase?

question: Can I split a line item's cost between material and labour?
answer_short: Yes. Use Split M/L to enter Material Cost and Labour Cost separately. FuzedFlow combines them into the Unit Cost.
answer_long:
On the quote line item, use **Split M/L** to enter **Material Cost** and **Labour Cost** separately. The two amounts combine into **Unit Cost**.

Check the quantity, client price, margin, and taxable setting after changing costs.

question: Can I choose which quote items are taxable?
answer_short: Yes. Each quote line item has its own Taxable setting.
answer_long: Yes. Each quote line item has its own Taxable setting.

question: What does Track Material do on a quote item?
answer_short: Track Material flags the line item as a material so it can later be imported into Project Materials.
answer_long:
Enable **Track Material** on a quote line item when the item should be available for import into **Project Materials**. Add a supplier if known.

The project must be linked to the quote before importing. This flag identifies a material; it does not place an order with the supplier.

question: What reporting periods can I use?
answer_short: Reports include filtering for year-to-date, quarter-to-date, current month and last month.
answer_long: Reports include filtering for year-to-date, quarter-to-date, current month and last month.

question: What reports are available in FuzedFlow?
answer_short: The Reports area includes Sales & Revenue, Expense Report, Tax Summary and Invoice Aging.
answer_long: The Reports area includes Sales & Revenue, Expense Report, Tax Summary and Invoice Aging.

question: What can I store in the Resource Library?
answer_short: Use the Resource Library page for reusable company files such as flyers, licenses and blank forms; it is separate from Pricebook.
answer_long:
Open **Client Forms** in company navigation to reach the page headed **Resource Library**. It is separate from the Products/Pricebook page.

Use **Upload File** to store a clearly named flyer, license, certificate or blank form, with an optional project link. Confirm the uploaded file opens with **View**.

In Quote Builder, use the resource picker under **Attached Documents** to open **Company Resources**, select **Attach**, and save the quote. Attaching a form does not create a general electronic-signature workflow, and uploading a warranty document does not enable warranty claims. Project drawings belong in the project’s Plans & Elevations workflow.

question: How do I invite a team member?
answer_short: Owners and administrators save team invitations in Settings → Team Management. Verify the pending record and ask the colleague to join with the invited email.
answer_long:
1. Sign in as an **Owner** or **Admin**.
2. Open **Settings → Team Management** and **Invite Team Member**.
3. Enter the colleague’s **Full Name** and **Email Address**.
4. Choose a supported **Access Role** and the appropriate **Hourly Pay Rate**.
5. Select **Send Invite** and verify the pending member appears in the list.

A saved pending invitation and the screen’s success message do not prove that an invitation email was delivered. Ask the colleague to use the invited email on the company join/signup path; if an invitation email exists, they can follow that link. Do not have them create an unrelated company account.

Current invitations require an owner/admin and canonical roles. Use the detailed Team Management form if a legacy Team Settings screen offers Standard User.

question: Can I see pending team invitations?
answer_short: Yes. Owners and administrators can inspect and edit or cancel pending invitations in Settings → Team Management.
answer_long:
Open **Settings → Team Management** as an Owner or Admin. Search by the colleague’s name or email and review the pending record’s address and role.

Use the pending member’s edit action to correct the available invitation details, or cancel an obsolete invitation. The current detailed form does not provide a dedicated Resend Email action. A pending record confirms the invitation was saved; it does not confirm an email was delivered.

Ask the colleague to register with the exact invited email on the company join/signup path, and check any received invitation email and spam folder. If the email already belongs to another company, resolve that membership rather than repeating signup.

Pending invitations count toward the detailed invitation form’s user-limit check.

question: What team roles are available in FuzedFlow?
answer_short: FuzedFlow supports Owner, Admin, Project Manager, Office Staff, Employee, and Subcontractor roles.
answer_long:
FuzedFlow uses **Owner, Admin, Project Manager, Office Staff, Employee, and Subcontractor** roles.

- **Owner / Admin:** company administration and full access.
- **Project Manager:** operational access, subject to permissions.
- **Office Staff:** office modules, subject to permissions.
- **Employee / Subcontractor:** field tools in the Employee Portal.

Owners and admins manage invitations and access in **Settings → Team Management**. The older Team page may show a legacy Standard User label; use Team Management for current role options.

question: Why can't I add another team member?
answer_short: Your FuzedFlow plan can have a user limit. If you have reached that limit, another user cannot be added until capacity is available or the plan changes.
answer_long: Your FuzedFlow plan can have a user limit. If you have reached that limit, another user cannot be added until capacity is available or the plan changes.

question: Can I save a reusable phase or room template?
answer_short: Yes. FuzedFlow supports Phase/Room Templates containing scope and reusable line items.
answer_long: Yes. FuzedFlow supports Phase/Room Templates containing scope and reusable line items.

question: Can I save reusable quote templates?
answer_short: Yes. FuzedFlow supports reusable Quote Templates.
answer_long: Yes. FuzedFlow supports reusable Quote Templates.

question: Can I search my templates?
answer_short: Yes. The Templates page supports searching quote and phase templates.
answer_long: Yes. The Templates page supports searching quote and phase templates.

question: Do timesheets require approval?
answer_short: Completed shifts and manual missing-hour submissions are Pending until HR reviews them. Employees cannot edit or delete an existing shift from My Time Sheets.
answer_long:
Clocking out or selecting **Submit to HR** in **My Time Sheets → Submit Missing Hours** saves a completed entry as **Pending**.

Owners, administrators, and office staff with HR plan access review entries in **Human Resources → Timesheets**, then approve, reject, or adjust them.

If an existing entry is rejected or incorrect, ask HR to review it using **Adjust Timesheet**. The employee My Time Sheets form creates a new missing shift; it does not edit or resubmit an existing shift. Do not add a duplicate to correct a record without HR’s instructions.

Check the shift date, hours, and status. A My Pay estimate can include Pending hours and does not prove payroll was approved or issued.

question: Can I clock in and out in FuzedFlow?
answer_short: Yes. Timesheets support clock-in/clock-out as well as manual time entry.
answer_long:
1. Open **Employee Portal**.
2. Choose **Clock In**.
3. Start your time entry when work begins and clock out when you finish.
4. Review your hours under **My Time Sheets**.

Use the available manual entry tools when you need to record missed time. Check the project and date before submitting hours for review.

question: Can two people edit the same quote at the same time?
answer_short: Use one editor at a time; the current Quote Builder does not enforce an automatic editing lock.
answer_long:
To avoid overwriting each other’s changes:

1. Agree who is editing the quote.
2. Have that person save their changes before handing it over.
3. Reload the quote before the next person starts editing.

The current Quote Builder does not enforce an automatic editing lock.

question: How do I create a new lead?
answer_short: Open Lead Tracker, choose New Lead, enter the details, and select Create Lead.
answer_long:
1. Open **Lead Tracker**.
2. Select **New Lead**.
3. Enter the required first name and surname, then contact details and the site address.
4. Set the pipeline stage, assignee, and follow-up date as needed.
5. Select **Create Lead**.

Owners, admins, and permitted managers/office staff receive an in-app creation notification, including the creator.

question: How do I filter project tasks by the person assigned?
answer_short: In Staff & Tasks, open Task List and choose a person under Assigned to.
answer_long:
1. Open **PM Projects** and select the project.
2. Choose **Staff & Tasks**, then **Task List**.
3. Use **Assigned to** to choose a team member.
4. Choose **Unassigned** to find tasks without an assignee.
5. Select **All users** or **Clear filter** to show the complete list again.

Tasks assigned to multiple people appear for each matching person. Filtering does not change the assignments.

question: Where do I find my notifications?
answer_short: Use the notification bell for alerts allowed by your company, event, role, permissions, and assigned work.
answer_long:
1. Tap the **notification bell** in the top navigation.
2. Choose **Unread**, or **All** to include read history.
3. Use **Mentions**, **Projects**, **Financial**, or **Action Required** to narrow the list.
4. Select an alert to read it and open its related record when a destination is available.

Visibility depends on the event’s permitted roles, module access, company, and project or personal assignment. Financial events do not all have one identical role rule; eligible managers can receive some quote or assigned-project financial updates, while other invoice/payment events are more restricted.

If **Notify me only when action is required** is on, Important and FYI updates remain hidden even in All. Turn it off to include them again. In-app alerts do not by themselves prove email, SMS, or native phone push delivery.

question: Who receives a notification when a lead is created?
answer_short: Owners, admins, and managers or office staff with Leads access receive the alert, including the creator.
answer_long:
A saved new lead generates an **Action Required** in-app notification for owners, admins, and eligible managers/office staff with Leads access. The creator is included when they are eligible.

Open the notification bell and choose **Unread** or **All**. The alert links to the new lead. Updating the same lead does not repeat its creation alert. Employees and subcontractors do not receive general company lead alerts.

question: How do I show only notifications that need action?
answer_short: Turn on Notify me only when action is required in the notification panel settings.
answer_long:
1. Open the **notification bell**.
2. Open the panel’s **settings** button.
3. Turn on **Notify me only when action is required**.

This filters both the list and unread badge. Important and FYI updates are hidden, not deleted. Turn the preference off to see them again. This is your personal in-app preference; company email and SMS settings are separate.

question: How do I mark notifications as read or find older alerts?
answer_short: Open an alert to read it, or use Mark this view read. Choose All for read and unread history.
answer_long:
Open a notification to mark it read and go to its related record. You can also use **Mark this view read** for the current filtered view.

Choose **All** to include read notifications. Use **Next** and **Previous** to move through older pages. Changing your action-only preference can reveal previously hidden alerts.

question: Why am I not seeing an expected notification?
answer_short: Check your notification filters, personal action-only setting, role, and assignment.
answer_long:
1. Open the bell and choose **All**.
2. Check whether **Notify me only when action is required** is on.
3. Confirm you have access to the relevant module or are assigned to the work.
4. Allow the app to refresh; it also checks for updates about once a minute.

If the alert is still missing, contact support with the event, record name, and approximate time. Do not include passwords or payment details.

question: Are in-app notifications the same as phone push notifications?
answer_short: No. The current notification centre provides in-app alerts; it does not add native phone push notifications.
answer_long:
The bell displays notifications while you use FuzedFlow. A new notification centre alert does not by itself send a native phone push notification.

Company email and SMS settings are separate. Do not rely on an in-app alert as confirmation that a phone push, text, or email was sent.

question: Can I manage warranty claims in FuzedFlow?
answer_short: FuzedFlow does not currently provide a complete dedicated warranty-claim workflow.
answer_long:
You can keep relevant project notes and documents, but FuzedFlow does not currently provide a complete dedicated warranty-claim intake, assignment, tracking, and resolution workflow.

Contact support if you need help finding an existing project record. Do not treat a project note as confirmation that a warranty claim has been formally submitted.

question: Does document approval capture an electronic signature?
answer_short: Quote/change-order approval and general document e-signing are different workflows.
answer_long:
FuzedFlow supports quote and change-order approval. It does not currently provide a complete general document e-signing and signature-tracking workflow.

Do not treat a document approval notification as proof that a signed document was captured. Use your agreed signing process when a signature is required.

question: How do I find help for a feature?
answer_short: Search the Knowledge Base & FAQ or choose a topic.
answer_long:

2. Search using a feature name or a few keywords.
3. Choose a topic to narrow the results.
4. Open a question to read the steps and follow **Open related page** where available.

question: How do I contact FuzedFlow support?
answer_short: Use Contact support to prepare an email draft, email support@fuzedflow.com, or call 1-855-400-3000.
answer_long:
Open **Help → Contact support**. Enter a subject and describe the page and issue, then select **Open email app**. Review the draft and send it from your email app.

If no email app opens, copy **support@fuzedflow.com** into your email service. You can also call **1-855-400-3000**. Published support hours are Monday–Friday, 8 AM–5 PM Mountain Time.

Leave out passwords and payment card details.

question: Where are the video tutorials?
answer_short: Video tutorials are coming soon. Use the Knowledge Base & FAQ for the current written guidance.
answer_long: The **Video tutorials** page is a coming-soon page. Use **Knowledge Base & FAQ** for written instructions or **Contact support** for help with a specific task.

question: How do I start a quote?
answer_short: Open Quotes, select New Quote, add the client, phases, and line items, then save the draft.
answer_long:
1. Open **Quotes** and choose **New Quote**.
2. Select the client and enter the quote details.
3. Use **Add Phase** to organize the scope of work.
4. Add line items and review quantities, costs, margin, taxes, and client prices.
5. Select **Save Draft** before previewing or sending the quote.

Use **Actions** to send by email or text after checking the final details.

question: Where can I see my assigned projects and schedule?
answer_short: Open Employee Portal and choose My Projects or My Schedule.
answer_long:
1. Open **Employee Portal**.
2. Choose **My Projects** to see assigned work.
3. Choose **My Schedule** for your scheduled work.
4. Use **My Tasks** to review tasks assigned to you.

If work is missing, ask your manager to check the assignment and company settings.

question: Where do I change company settings?
answer_short: Authorized owners, admins, and managers use Settings; available sections depend on the role.
answer_long:
Open **Settings** and choose a section using the sidebar or the mobile **Settings Section** selector. Sections include branding, quote customization, message templates, financial settings, payments, notifications, and portal controls.

Owners and admins have full administration access. Managers see a limited set of sections. If a setting is not available, ask your company administrator.

question: Can I connect QuickBooks from Settings?
answer_short: The current QuickBooks connection action is marked Coming soon.
answer_long: The current **QuickBooks** connection action in Settings displays **Coming soon**. Do not assume invoices or payments are synchronizing with QuickBooks. Keep using your existing accounting process until an active integration is available.

question: Where do I manage vendors and subcontractors?
answer_short: Vendors is the company subcontractor/supplier directory; the project Subcontractors area manages project assignments. Directory access is restricted.
answer_long:
Open **Vendors** for the **Subcontractors Directory**, including contact information, categories, preferred status, project history, supporting files, and internal notes.

For a specific job, open **PM Projects → Open → Subcontractors** to create or review a project assignment. A directory record or project-history tag does not itself schedule a subcontractor for a job. Phase-level assignment is available under the project's **Phases** area.

The global directory has an access check. If your account shows **Access Denied**, ask a company administrator to review that access rather than assuming the directory is empty. On mobile, directory creation and import actions are in the top **Actions** menu.

question: Where do I manage tasks?
answer_short: Use Tasks for general work, Staff & Tasks for a project, or My Tasks in the Employee Portal.
answer_long:
- **Tasks:** general task management for authorized office and project staff.
- **PM Projects → your project → Staff & Tasks:** work linked to that project, including the **Assigned to** filter.
- **Employee Portal → My Tasks:** tasks assigned to the field user.

Check the assignee, due date, status, and project before saving changes.

question: Getting started with FuzedFlow
answer_short: Find your workspace, understand your role, and follow your first workflow from the correct starting point.
answer_long:
## Choose the correct workspace
If you are joining an existing company, use the invitation sent by its administrator. Creating a separate company account does not automatically put you on that company's team. Sign in using the same method you used when joining: email and password, or **Sign in with Google**.

Office and project staff normally begin in the main workspace. Employees and subcontractors use the **Employee Portal**. The menu reflects your role and your company's permissions; a missing menu item does not mean your work was deleted.

## Start with your role
1. Open the navigation menu. On a phone, use the menu button at the top left.
2. For office work, start with **Leads**, **Clients**, or **Quotes**. Check the client and site before creating a document.
3. For project coordination, use **PM Dashboard**, **PM Projects**, or **Project Timeline**.
4. For field work, open **Employee Portal** and choose the relevant section, such as **Clock In**, **My Projects**, or **My Tasks**.
5. Owners and administrators can review company branding, financial defaults, notifications, and team access in **Settings** before sending customer documents.

## Follow a complete workflow
A typical office workflow moves from lead information to a client, then to a quote, project work, and invoicing. These are separate records and actions. Changing a lead stage does not by itself prove that a quote was accepted, a project was created, or an invoice was paid.

Before sending or approving a document, check its record number, recipient, project, and preview. Return to its list after saving and confirm that the new record or status appears.

## Find help without leaving your task
Use **Help → Help Articles** in the top navigation. Search for the screen name or the action you need, open a guide, and use its related-page link where available. **Quick answers & FAQ** offers shorter answers. AI Help can explain the same published articles and link you back to a guide.

## If access or records are missing
Confirm that you signed into the intended company account, clear active list filters, and ask your administrator to check your role or assignments. Keep the page name and any error text when contacting support. Never send passwords or payment card details.

question: Using FuzedFlow on a phone or tablet
answer_short: Navigate the mobile menu, read guides, and keep track of work when space is limited.
answer_long:
## Open the mobile navigation
Use the menu button at the top left to open the sidebar. Office navigation groups related screens under **CRM**, **Quotes**, **Project Management**, **Financial**, and **Resources**. Tap a group to reveal its pages, then tap the page you want. Selecting a page closes the sidebar so your workspace is visible again.

The exact options depend on your role. Field users work through **Employee Portal** rather than the office navigation. Turning the device sideways may make a wide table easier to inspect, but does not change your permissions.

## Find help from any supported workspace
1. Tap **Help** in the top navigation.
2. Choose **Help Articles** for detailed instructions or **Quick answers & FAQ** for a short answer.
3. Enter a screen name or a few useful words in the search field.
4. Narrow the topic or article type if there are many matches.
5. Open an article and use **Jump to section** to reach the part you need.

The portal uses large search and filter controls and wraps article text within the screen. Long lists load in groups; use **Show more** rather than expecting every article to appear at once.

## Work with forms and lists
Before saving, review fields above and below the keyboard. Close the keyboard when you need more room to inspect a form. Scroll within a table if a screen provides horizontal scrolling, and check that an action belongs to the intended row before tapping it.

If a list looks empty, clear its search, date, status, project, or assignee filters. A mobile section selector may replace the tabs or sidebar shown on desktop; look for the section name above the content.

## Use AI Help comfortably
Tap the yellow **AI Help** button. Type one task or issue at a time and include the page name. Answers support numbered steps, readable lists, and related article links. Follow a related article to read the longer explanation. Close the helper to return to your work.

## If the page is difficult to use
Save or copy your unfinished text before refreshing. Try closing an open menu or keyboard, then reopen the section. If a control still cannot be reached, note the page, device/browser, and what you were trying to do when contacting support. A screenshot of the layout can help; leave private customer and payment details out.

question: Troubleshooting missing records, failed actions, and loading problems
answer_short: Use a practical checklist to resolve common issues and give support the details it needs when a problem remains.
answer_long:
## First check the current state
Before repeating an action, confirm what actually happened. A toast or changed label alone may not prove that an email was delivered, a payment was collected, or another record was updated. Return to the record list, reopen the item, and check the saved values or status.

Keep unfinished form text somewhere safe before refreshing or navigating away. Avoid repeated payment, send, create, or approval clicks while a request is still running; duplicates are harder to diagnose.

## A record or task is missing
1. Confirm the company account and page you are using.
2. Clear search text and narrow filters, including dates, statuses, projects, and assignees.
3. Check other pages of a paginated list.
4. For field work, ask your manager to check the project/task assignment and enabled portal sections.
5. If a page is unavailable, ask an administrator to check role and permissions. Do not create a second company account to recover access.

## A page will not load
Check your connection. If the help page offers **Try again**, use that action first. If the problem persists, preserve your form details and refresh once. Sign in again if the app reports that your session has expired. Note whether one page fails or the whole workspace is affected.

## A save, upload, or send fails
Check required fields and the selected client/project. For uploads, keep the original file and note its type and size. Inspect the record list before repeating a creation action. For a send action, check the recipient address and any saved delivery/status information; do not treat a status change as proof of external delivery.

Some pages include actions marked **Coming soon** or incomplete workflows. Search the article for that feature to check its current availability before trying again. A different entry point may have different capabilities, so include the exact page and action in your report.

## A document total or report looks wrong
Compare the source document, quantities, tax settings, selected options, and recorded payments. Review the customer-facing preview before sending. Do not infer payment collection or accounting synchronization from a dashboard figure alone.

## Give support a useful report
Open **Help → Contact support** and include the page, record number, expected result, actual result, error text, and steps already tried. Include the approximate time and device/browser. **Open email app** prepares a draft; review and send it from your mail app. Never include passwords, secret links, or full payment card information.

question: Finding pages and records with navigation and search
answer_short: Understand the navigation groups and use record search separately from help search.
answer_long:
## Understand the workspace menu
The office sidebar groups screens by job: **CRM** contains leads and clients; **Quotes** contains quotes and templates; **Project Management** contains project views and approvals; **Financial** includes the financial pages your role can access; and **Resources** includes tasks, products, inventory, project notes, forms, reports, and HR where permitted.

**Employee Portal** provides field tools. **Settings** is the company configuration entry point for authorized roles. On desktop the sidebar can collapse; on mobile the menu button opens it and group headings expand their pages.

## Search your business records
1. Use the search control in the top navigation. On desktop, **Ctrl+K** or **Command+K** toggles the search.
2. Enter part of a quote title/number, client name/email, lead name/email, project name/number, or invoice number.
3. Use the search filters when you need a particular record type, status, date range, or amount range.
4. Select a result to open its record view.
5. Press **Escape** or close search to return to the workspace.

Search uses records in the signed-in company. It is a shortcut to supported record types, rather than a search of every attachment or every word inside every document. A screen's own list search may offer a more specific way to find an item.

## Search instructions instead of records
Use **Help → Help Articles** to find instructions. Help search looks through article titles, summaries, text, topics, and keywords. Search for an action such as creating a quote, filtering assigned tasks, or recording time. Topic and article-type filters can narrow the results.

## If search returns no results
Try a shorter identifying term and clear filters. Confirm that the record is in the company you are signed into. Check its own page and pagination. If a result opens a page your role cannot access, ask your administrator to review access rather than changing the URL or assuming the record is gone.

## Keep page names with your question
Different records can have similar names. Include the screen name and record number when asking AI Help or support. For example, say whether you are searching the general **Tasks** screen or a project's **Staff & Tasks** list.

question: Understanding missing menu items and role-based access
answer_short: Recognize the difference between your role, company permissions, and work assignments.
answer_long:
## Access depends on your role
FuzedFlow uses **Owner**, **Admin**, **Project Manager**, **Office Staff**, **Employee**, and **Subcontractor** roles. Owners and administrators have broad company access. Managers and office staff use operational pages subject to their role and configured permissions. Employees and subcontractors are directed to the **Employee Portal** for field work.

The invoice and HR routes allow owners, administrators, and office staff; managers do not automatically have those routes. Company settings is available to owners, administrators, and managers, with a smaller set of settings shown to managers. A menu label by itself does not override a page's access rules.

## Diagnose a missing section
1. Confirm that you joined the intended company using its invitation.
2. Check whether you are in the office workspace or Employee Portal.
3. Ask an administrator to review your current role and permissions.
4. For field work, also check project/task assignments and enabled portal features.
5. Sign out and back in if your administrator changed access and the screen still shows old options.

Permission checks and assignment checks answer different questions: permission controls whether a tool is available; assignment controls which work is relevant to you. Neither guarantees that every record appears under the active list filters.

## Read help for your access level
Signed-in company users can open Help Articles, FAQ, tutorials, and Contact support. The portal hides admin-only content from non-admin roles. Field users receive field-related topics and general help rather than the full office library. AI Help uses the same access rules when choosing articles.

## Avoid creating a second account as a workaround
A new company registration does not restore membership or assignments in the existing company. Ask the administrator who invited you to confirm the email, role, and invitation status. Keep your existing account details private.

## When an access error continues
Send support the page name and the message shown, along with the role you expect to have. Leave passwords and invitation links out of the message. Support can help investigate the screen, while your company administrator remains the contact for deciding the access you should receive.

question: Reviewing quotes, change orders, and purchase orders in Approvals
answer_short: Choose the approval record type, review its status, and distinguish approvals from document signing and delivery.
answer_long:
## Choose the record type
Open **Approvals** from Project Management. Use the view selector to choose **Quote Approvals**, **Change Orders**, or **Purchase Orders**. Each view uses its own search and status filters, so an empty list may simply reflect the selected view or filter.

This is an office/project coordination screen. Field users should ask their manager about approval status rather than expect the Approvals page in the Employee Portal.
